content.text:
I submitted index 25 (Mn 0.49 / Sr 0.51) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 4.26 µA. I can't tell how close that is to the best composition in the library, because the other 26 were never measured.

| Index | Mn / Sr | Photocurrent | Why I picked it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25 | 0.49 / 0.51 | **4.26 µA** | SrMnO3 has the widest predicted band gap, about 1.8 eV |
| 20 | 0.57 / 0.43 | 3.08 µA | The statistical model ranked it top; tests the Mn-rich side of index 25 |
| 16 | 0.38 / 0.62 | 0.07 µA | Sr7Mn4O15 is stable with a predicted gap of 1.64 eV, but its photocurrent was almost nil |

**Why I skipped the Mn-rich end (Mn above 0.8):** the phase expected there, SrMn7O12, is predicted to be nearly metallic (gap 0.04 eV), so it shouldn't produce much photocurrent. SrMn2O6 has a large predicted gap (2.78 eV), but the stability model says it's unlikely to form. That region was never measured, so this is a judgement from predictions, not a result.

**Gaps:**
- With the photocurrent dropping on both sides of index 25, the peak is probably near Mn 0.5. But index 24 (Mn 0.52) and index 22 (Mn 0.47) are close by and untested, and either could be slightly higher.
- I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so I haven't checked which phases actually formed in the films.
